articleTitle: Highest Efficiency and Super Quality Audio Amplifier using MOS Power FETS in Class G Operation
abstract: A Class "G" audio power amplifier has achieved a rated continuous output power of 200 watts and peak power of 400 watts. This power amplifier produced no more than 0.01 per cent total harmonic distortion at 20 kHz and 200 watts by using Power MOS FETs in its output stage.

articleTitle: Video Cassette Recorder Development for Consumers
abstract: The first 2-head, helical scan type color video tape recorder appeared on the scene 18 years ago. Since that time numerous technical innovations have made possible an increase in the recording density, development of new color recording systems, utilization of cassette tapes, and so forth. Based on these achievements, a video cassette recorder designed and developed especially for home usage has recently met with completion and this system has been named "VHS".

articleTitle: A Fully Automatic Ghost Canceller
abstract: Ghost may be one of the largest remnaining causes of picture degradations as TV broadcast and receiver's quality increases rapidly. Even the best antennas are not always adequate to remove ghosts. Most of the existing systems are not practical because they must be readjusted for each channel and different meteorogical conditions.

articleTitle: 30AX Self-Aligning 110°In-Line Color TV Display
abstract: 30AX is a new in-line color TV display system with 110 deflection angle and interchangeable tubes and yokes. It is based on the production experience gained with the 20AX system introduced in 19741,2,3) and the results of further investigation in the field of tube technology and deflection yoke design. For the tube, this meant a new reference system, an internal magnetic correction ring and an improved gun design. For the yoke, the most important elements are a new "flangeless" winding technology, a change in the shape of the windings at the screen side of the line deflection coil and the use of field shapers embedded in the deflection coil.

articleTitle: UHF Taboos-History and Development
abstract: This paper details the origin and application of the UHF "Taboos," mileage restraints that are the basis for allocation of TV channels in the UHF spectrum by the FCC.

articleTitle: New Color TV Receiver With SAW IF Filter
abstract: It is always our old and new subject that we must kill two birds, performance improvement and cost reduction, with one stone.

articleTitle: The "High Voltage Bipotential" Approach to Enhanced Color Tube Performance
abstract: Recent developments in high performance electron guns for color Tv include a high focus voltage bipotential design -commonly called "hi bi" -designed primarily for 29-mm neck, inline applications. The improved spot size capability of this design, together with its simplicity and cost effectiveness for the set maker, make this system a strong contender for color applications up to at least 19V diagonal sizes.

articleTitle: A New Design Technique, for Digital PLL Synthesizers
Advanced and Simplified Signal Processing System for VTR and Its High Performance LSI'S
abstract: The Video Tape Recorder(VTR) may be the most complex appliance among home electronic appliances. The number of electronic parts used totals more than 1,400 peaces, even many ICs are involved. For this reason, to ensure reliability and performance is difficult in comparison with other home appliances.

articleTitle: A Complete AM/FM Signal Processing System
abstract: This paper describes a monolithic integrated circuit which makes possible substantial simplification of AM/FM receiver design, while at the same time improving system performance.

articleTitle: A Rotary-Head PCM Recorder Employing Error Correction Technique
abstract: A digital audio system now includes a home use VTR as record and reproduce media. In this system, audio signal is converted into digital codes by PCM, which are again converted such that the resultant signal be identical with NTSC TV format. This insures ready use of existing TV equipments, their peripherals, and networks.

articleTitle: High Performance Receiver
abstract: This paper discusses a new high performance television tuner/IF recently developed by Texas Instruments and deliered to the FCC in engineering model form for evaluation. The project effectively demonstrated that new device technologies in conjunction with a system that takes advantage of such new technologies can be utilized to greatly improve TV receiver performance over that which is currently realized. The theory of operation, system architecture, new component technology, actual circuitry used, and final performance of the new receiver system will all be presented in this paper.

articleTitle: VIR II System
abstract: The quality of color reproduction in color television receivers has often suffered due to the misadjustment of chroma level and tint controls by the customer. To give some help to the customer, several schemes have been introduced such as automatic chroma level, automatic tint, and factory preset controls, These systems are widely used, but do not solve the problems caused by chroma level or subcarrier phase differences between stations or control voltage drift during warm-up period. Moreover, factory preset controls are subject to drift from their original setting due to component aging and eventually should be set again, which requires a service call. Therefore, a better system which is not subject to these problems become desirable. In October, 1975, after several years of testing by the broadcasting industry and the EIA, the FCC designated the 19th line of each field of video information as reserved for a specific Vertical Interval Reference (VIR) signal. The signal itself simply consists of a chroma reference, a luminance reference, and a black level reference as shown in Fig. 1. When the chrominance reference and black level reference are equal in amplitude at the receiver's R-Y output, chroma phase (tint) conforms to that of the transmitted reference signal. Likewise, by maintaining proper amplitude relationship between the B-Y output and the luminance signal, chroma level can be matched to the reference signal. The use of this VIR signal has finally provided the color television receivers with the means for truly automatic chroma level and tint reception.

articleTitle: A Phase-Tracking Loop (PTL) Detector for FM Signals and its Application to an FM Receiver
abstract: High-Fidelity demodulation of FM signals requires a wide frequency range with low distortion, and sufficient protection from interference. However, these two requirements are incompatible each other, i.e. a wide band detector accepts interference simultaneously with the desired signal. Current increase of FM broadcasting stations aggravates this problem.

articleTitle: Internal Surge Limiting for Picture Tubes
abstract: Despite the application of modern manufacturing methods and rigid quality control procedures at each step of the process, TV picture tubes operated at present-day receiver anode voltages may occasionally produce a high voltage arcover. With receivers now being constructed with 100-percent semiconductor active elements, a flashover may, if the circuitry is not adequately designed, result in catastrophic failure somewhere in the unit or in interference to low level circuits, such as memory tuning systems.

articleTitle: Surface Acoustic Wave Devices for Use in a High Performance Television Tuner*
abstract: Two key components in a high performance tuner/IF system for television are described; a surface acoustic wave (SAW) low loss filter and a surface acoustic wave resonator. The low loss filter provides the adjacent channel rejection and ultimate spurious signal suppression with accurate amplitude and phase control that are the cornerstones for the high performance receiver. The resonator is the frequency control element for a stable, low-cost local oscillator for down converting the TV signal after it is cleaned up by the fixed frequency low loss filter. In this paper the characteristics of the SAW ccnponents are described.

articleTitle: Super High Quality FM Detector and its Development Process
abstract: An FM ratio detector has achieved signal-to-noise ratio of better than 90 dB and T.H.D. of less than 0.01% using a lower load factor and a new arrangement of detector coils with an index of coupling of 1.2 selected.

articleTitle: A Highly Stable Integrated Sync System
abstract: Television receivers have used integrated sync systems for several years. Both LC, and more recently, RC horizontal oscillators have been employed which offer stable performance in one or two chip horizontal/vertical systems.3 However, in each case at least one adjustment has been required for the oscillator frequencies. This paper will present a highly stable one chip horizontal/vertical sync system which no longer needs any frequency adjustment.

articleTitle: Low-Cost Digital Tunung System with Full-Function Automatic Search Preset
abstract: One of the most widely used tuning system in the USA at present is a one-knob rotary channel selector, which presets TV channels with potentiometers, and selects them with a mechanical rotary switch. But in this system we need the experienced adjustment labor and devoted time in order to preset the exact tuning point with potentiometers.

articleTitle: An AM-FM Digital Tuning System
abstract: Digital tuning system approaches to AM-FM broadcast receivers are becoming increasingly popular as manufacturers are finding lower component costs and increased features give their products greater appeal. Operational features of a digitally tuned receiver include: • Precise tuning of station frequency • Display of exact receive frequency • Keyboard entry of station frequency • Storage of multiple stations in memory • Pushbutton up/down scan through the band • Pushbutton search (stop on next station) • Power on to last station • Provision for time of day clock • Static drive of LED for noise-free operation • Able to address CB synthesizer

articleTitle: An Integrated FM Front-End Interface for Radio Receivers
abstract: A new integrated circuit further expanding capabilities of the Integrated FM Front End chip, introduced three years ago, is described, and a new AFC action principle is introduced. Also, a novel tuning system configuration providing optimum performance of the new integrated circuit is proposed.

articleTitle: Frequency Synthesis Tuning Systems With Automatic Offset Tuning
abstract: This paper describes a new closed-loop tuning system utilizing custom large scale integrated circuits to control the selection of the 82 U.S. television channels. The system is designed to minimize hardware but yet support multiple user features. No frequency adjustment or prealignment is needed for operation. A crystal frequency reference is continually used on each channel, but full compatibility with automatic fine tuning is maintained to cope with transmitters operating off FCC assigned frequencies. Channel selection is easily remoted and is either by digital keyboard or by up-down scan of a user selected list of channels stored in non-volatile digital memory. Channel number display is either on screen with time of day or off screen using a digital display.

articleTitle: Microprocessor Based, Software Defined Television Controller
A New Optical Videodisc System with One Hour Playing Time
abstract: A series of papers proposing a possible format for reflection-type optical videodisc systems was published in 19761-3. Principal parameters of the format (with NTSC standards) are as follows: the disc rotation speed is 1800 rpm, the track-to-track pitch is 1.67m, and the playing time is 30 minutes from one side of a 12-inch-diameter disc. A direct frequency modulation of the composite NTSC video signal is employed, with the attractive feature that the full extent (4.2 MHz) of NTSC luminance bandwidth can be retained in this format.

articleTitle: Chroma Systems Trend in the Past and Future and Latest Chroma IC with Versatile Flexibility
abstract: Chroma circuit is one of the most important parts in a color television set. Figure 1 shows the history of chroma systems focusing the change of active devices and the quantity of parts.s

articleTitle: A New Magnetic-Focus Static-Deflection System for a Sincle-Tube Color Camera
abstract: The need for high quality electron optical systems for small size color camera has remarkedly increased since the advent of compact VTRs. A new magnetic-focus static-deflection system has been developed under a program of exploration of possibilities of designing vidicon tubes. The objective is to make a focusing and deflection system which will have high quality electron optical characteristics with simple construction and require low power consumption. The main characteristics required are small focus spot size, scan linearity and normal beam landing. The beam landing angle affects shading, resolution, lag and flicker of camera tubes which employ low-velocity electron beam [1]. The normal beam landing performance is essential especially for a single tube color camera system in order to read out coded color signals with accuracy.

articleTitle: A Bilateral Analog FET Optocoupler
abstract: Recently, optoelectronic switches for low-level applications were described by Bussolati (1) and Brown (2). The optoelectronic switch proposed in Bussolati's paper consists of two phototransistors (PT) connected back-to-back with separate infrared emitting diodes (IRED's). Although by varying the ratio of the currents in the IRED's the offset voltage of the switch can then be zeroed, it is not a very practical device to use. An excellent performance, but technically complex and relatively costly hybrid to perform the same circuit function is detailed in Brown's paper. It is the purpose of this paper to present a new device called an optically-coupled bilateral analog FET, which is an economically advantageous design with technical trade-offs compared to the previous devices. This new device features a monolithic detector, coupled to an IRED, and is newly available in sample quantities. It provides the function of an ideal bilateral analog FET with isolated current control of the output conductance. This provides the advantage of optical isolation to the analog electronic functions of a linear, electronically variable, resistor (from 20 ohms to hundreds of megohms) and a fast bilateral ac low-level signal switch. The IRED and the detector are enclosed in a 6-pin DIP, although other configurations are possible. The structure and characteristics of this device are described in this paper. Possible applications, as well as limitations, are thoroughly analyzed.

articleTitle: Soft-Flash Picture Tubes
abstract: Between the gun electrodes of picture tubes, high electric field strengths are present. In a typical color picture tube there is a voltage difference of some 20 kV across a gap of about 1 mm, between the focus electrode and the anode of the gun. Although the utmost precautions are taken in the design and manufacture of the tube, there is always a chance that a flashover will eventually occur. When it does, the discharge current rapidly reaches a very high value, inducing voltages throughout the receiver chassis which may destroy semiconductors. Even with the most careful circuit layout, complete protection is difficult to ensure.

articleTitle: Development of the PCM Laser Sound Disc Player
abstract: The authors studied dropout characteristics of optical disc player and based on the results of the dropout measurements, we determined one format which recorded and reproduced digitalized stereo audio signal which was frequency modulated.

articleTitle: New Voltage Regulators Integrate More Functions, Have Wider Applications Field
abstract: The present state of the art in linear integrated circuits enables more complex functions to be realized and therefore offers users either greater economy or greater device reliability and performance.

articleTitle: New Developments in Integrated Horizontal Processors for TV
abstract: In order to overcome the problem of vertical and horizontal sync incompatibility, a new horizontal deflection IC has been developed.

articleTitle: Digital Amplifiers for Analog Power
abstract: A design using highly efficient switchmode power amplifiers enables the engineer to offer extended battery life to portable equipment, reduce heat sinking requirements, and offer considerable energy savings. There are over a million audio amplifiers in the city of Chicago alone. If we could save a mere one watt per amplifier we will have saved over a million valuable watts!

articleTitle: Remote-Controlled TV Receiver Using a Digital Tuning System
abstract: Together with very fast dividers and a PLL system it is possible to digitally process the oscillator frequencies of a TV tuner. With this method you can set up a tuning system which remembers a once programmed channel with a resolution that was up till now reserved only for costly and highly professional equipment. The control commands for this system are derived from an infrared remote control that links to the tuning system.

articleTitle: A Microcomputer to Consumer Color TV Interface IC Chip
abstract: A MOS/LSI IC to interface a microcomputer to a consumer color television has been designed. It generates an interlaced composite video (Y) and the two color components (RY and BY) to display two intensity and eight color displays in a standard NTSC color receiver. The chip can be configured in one of the fourteen modes of operation, most of which can be switched among themselves on the fly on one screen. Of the fourteen modes, four are alphanumeric, which display 512 characters (16 rows of 32 characters) per screen from an internal (on chip) or external read only memory (ROM). Two semigraphic modes (resolution 64 ×32 and 64 ×48) give the programmer limited graphic capability. The eight graphics modes range in resolution from 64 ×64 to 256 ×192. The chip is designed for easy interface with most 8 bit microprocessors. All refresh memory updating by the CPU is done during vertical retrace and hence is transparent to the screen.

articleTitle: A New LSI Integrated Circuit for Line Recognition and VIR Signal Processing in Television Receivers
abstract: The Vertical Interval Reference (VIR) signal transmitted on line 19 of each field of the NTSC composite video signal is being used in an increasing number of television receivers for control of color and tint of the displayed picture. These receivers contain circuitry that recognizes each line 19, detects the presence of a VIR signal, and processes the VIR signal to produce error signals to control the chrominance circuitry.

articleTitle: A Sixteen-Color Composite Video Summer Integrated Circuit for Video Display Terminals and Game Systems
abstract: This paper describes a monolithic video summer developed by Signetics for video display terminals and game systems capable of accepting NTSC timing signals and a four bit binary code to generate up to 16 separate composite video signals as well as a T2L compatible 3.58 MHz square wave output for genlock or game countdown systems. Video switching speeds and color phase accuracy superior to many competitor products have been achieved. The system concept, basic circuit building blocks, application innovations, and typical performance criteria will all be presented in this paper.

articleTitle: Frequency Synthesis Custom LSI: The Inside Story
abstract: The heart of the Frequency Synthesizer System is an N-MOS custom LSI which contains the reference oscillator, programmable divider, phase locked loop, mode control logic, and the control-interface logic. The IC contains two sections. The tuner control section which is involved with the tuning loop, and the control-interface section which is involved with the overall operation of the system and the interface of the system to the user. The section of the IC associated with the tuning loop will be described in the second half of this paper.

articleTitle: One-Chip-Controlled Voltage Synthesizer Tv Tuning System
abstract: There are several varieties of TV electronic tuning systems., e.g., potentiometer, voltage synthesizer and frequency synthesizer tuning systems. Usually a potentiometer system is adopted, but it needs many components such as potentiometers, switches for band selection and etc. Although a frequency synthesizer system features accurate tuning, it requires high speed logic circuits.

articleTitle: Second Generation IC's for Color TV Receivers (Part II)
abstract: Second Generation IC's with high performances for color TV's have newly been developed and now put into actual use. The IC's consist of five big IC's, which are for VIF, SIF audio, video chroma, jungle and horizontal and vertical oscillators, and vertical output. These five packages of IC's cover all the circuitry that can be designed into IC's with advantage and reduced component counts of a color TV receiver typically from 500 to 300 which is comparable with that of a black and white TV, and reduced assembly and adjustment time by 35 to 40%, resulting in ease of production and improved reliability.

articleTitle: The Physical Mechanisms of Feedback Multiplier Electron Sources
A Versatile Low-Level Luminance IC for TV
abstract: The low level luminance I.C. that is described in this paper is designed to have multiple features and flexibility in its application to TV receivers. Thus, versatility is stressed in the design rather than the minimization of the pin count for the package. The I.C. Chip is fabricated with bi polar technology and is housed in an 18 pin dual in-line plastic package. It is intended for use with a +24V power supply.

articleTitle: A Jumbo for Vertical Deflection and Video Signal Processing Circuits in TV Receiver
abstract: A monolithic single chip IC for TV vertical deflection and video signal processing circuits has been successfully developed. The IC incorporates video pre-amplifier, noise canceller, sync separator, horizontal AFC, horizontal oscillator, vertical integrator, vertical oscillator and vertical deflection amplifier with vertical output stage. The 118 ×114 mil chip, containing 107 transistors, 25 diodes, 157 resistors and 4 capacitors, is sealed in a 24 pin dual-in-line power package. The allowable maximum power dissipation of this IC is 2.1 watts at an ambient temperature of 70 °C, therefore this IC can be used in a 12" B/W TV receiver without an additional heat sink.

articleTitle: Feedback Multiplier Flat-Panel Technologies
abstract: The flat panel television system described in the two previous papers includes conventional materials and processes as well as new ones. The technologies peculiar to this display are described in this report.

articleTitle: Contoured-Line Screens for Color Picture Tubes
An Interference-Rejection AM Receiver
abstract: The last ten years has seen a fantastic increase in the public's enthusiasm for high-fidelity audio equipment. "Stereo" is a word that everyone knows, even if they don't know the meaning. FM broadcasting has reached its heyday after decades of neglect, and AM radio is losing much of its audience to FM because of the public's desire for stereo and the good fidelity reception which FM offers. This is occuring in spite of the fact that AM broadcast offers several advantages over FM, such as freedom from multipath and shadowing and wide range night time coverage. The audience now desires good fidelity.

articleTitle: LED Displays Past, Present, Future
abstract: Solid state displays have made solid progress in the last few years. Colors, sizes, brightness and costs have made significant progress with much more progress expected in the near future.

articleTitle: New Power Supply for Audio Power Amplifiers
abstract: A switch-mode power supply was developped to meet requirement for reduction in size and weight for high power amplifiers.

articleTitle: Better Internal Protection and Fewer Leads Mark New Generation of Integrated L-F Power Amplifiers
abstract: The new device incorporates interesting soluations for its protection, uses an economic, well-proven plastic power package and offers hi-fi performance even under full-load conditions. It can work as a DC amplifier with a single or split power supply. The output power is 20W or 13W with THD 0.5% when it drives loads of 4 or 8 respectively.

articleTitle: Single Chip Deflection System IC for Color TV
abstract: Deflection system in a color TV consists of a sync separator, vertical and horizontal oscillators, and an AFC circuit. Several devices to perform these functions have been developed. Stringent requirements of frequency stability necessiated the development of sophisticated devices such as AFC and frequency count down IC's.

articleTitle: An LSI Approach for Achieving Easy Play Organ Features
abstract: Early organ chord-bass systems usually lacked the intelligence and foresight to provide unrestricted musical performance. This article describes a recently-developed system which remedies those earlier problems via the use of custom LSI.

articleTitle: UHF TV Tuner using PC Board with Suspended Striplines
abstract: A high performance varactor-tuned UHF tuner using epoxy-glass laminate in resonant circuits was developed. Noise figure of below 6 dB and image rejection ratio of above 70 dB were obtained.

articleTitle: Consumer Electronics and the Commission
abstract: An enormous variety of electronic apparatus is now offered for sale to the public. Such devices may cause, or be susceptible to, electromagnetic interference. Proliferation of these goods with no control over their radio interference qualities would result in a chaotic environment: not all devices could be enjoyed as the inventor planned because of mutual or self-interference.

articleTitle: Nine-Band, 81-Channel Remote-Controlled Broadcast Receiver
abstract: A simple remote control system providing the six FM programs and three TV sound channels available in this area to all rooms in the authors home had been operating satisfactorily for a year.

articleTitle: A Low Cost Varactor Tuning System for Television
Wide-Range and High Efficiency Switching Power Supply for Color TV Receivers
abstract: In TV receivers with semiconductors, regulated power supplies are necessary to keep reliable operation of the receivers, against both the source voltage fluctuation and load variation. Generally its regulated DC output voltage is constrained around 100V by a horizontal output transistor rating.

articleTitle: Using a One-Chip Microprocessor for TV Tuning and Remote Control
abstract: While many types of electronic tuning systems have been suggested and tried and several are being produced and sold, all have been custom designs; dedicated I.C.'s having long design cycles and costly tooling. By the time the TV manufacturer receives the first sample custom I.C.'s he may discover that the features originally proposed are no longer popular. The long-term investment, however, forces him to go into production with an obsolete design.

articleTitle: Flat TV Display Using Feedback Multipliers
Single-Chip Sound Channel Offers Greater Flexibility, More Functions
abstract: The TV consumer market trend is to offer a more and more sophisticated television set with an ever increasing number of functions.

articleTitle: Higher Integration for Tomorrow's Cassette/Tape Recorders
abstract: The continuing need to reduce assembly costs and bulk of consumer electronic equipments can still be satisfied by developing new integrated circuits to incorporate more functions and reduce external component requirements. This paper describes one such device which was designed for cassette/tape recorders and performs the functions of motor speed control, bias and erase oscillator, automatic and manual stop.

articleTitle: Electronically Switched Tape Audio Processor
Channel-Calculating Logic for a TV Tuning System
abstract: A digital television receiver tuning circuit has been developed. The circuit accepts multiplexed BCD channel numbers from any user control circuit providing data in that format. When a new channel is called for, the acquisition time is minimized by rapidly sweeping a voltage-controlled local oscillator until over-shoot of the desired frequency is detected and then switching to phase-locked-loop operation to achieve exact tuning. In the PLL mode, the local oscillator frequency is divided by a modulus that depends on the channel number. The logic provides a variable modulus by presetting a counter to a state common to all channels in the band and counting until a match to the desired channel number is obtained. Operation in the channel number domain substantially reduces the amount of ROM required in contrast to other techniques. The counter output is compared to a reference frequency and frequency/phase comparator output pulses produce changes in the tuning voltage to keep the local oscillator tuned to the standard channel frequency. Although PLL operation is adequate in most environments, nonstandard carrier frequencies must be accommodated. A local option switch permits release to a conventional AFC after the PLL has tuned exactly to the standard channel frequency. In the AFC mode, the digital system monitors the local oscillator and initiates a tuning cycle only if the frequency deviates from the standard frequency by a prescribed amount. Careful attention to speed considerations and partitioning have permitted this circuit to be achieved in a custom PMOS IC with only 18 pins.

articleTitle: Saw IF Filter on LITaO3 for Color TV Receivers
abstract: More than eight years have passed since DeVries et al. reported the first attempt at installing SAW (Surface Acoustic Wave) filters in a TV set(1). In Japan, SAW IF filter development has been continued by several companies and TV receivers incorporating SAW filter have been placed on the market since 1977.

articleTitle: A Systems Approach to Low-Cost Electronic Tuning Address
A Microcomputer Controlled Frequency Synthesizer for TV
abstract: This microcomputer controlled frequency synthesizer is a unique electronic television tuning system. It is a frequency synthesizer that always insures crystal stability by forcing the local oscillator in the tuner to assume the same stability as a fixed frequency crystal reference oscillator. Also, microcomputer controlled tuning provides many desireable features. The microcomputer controlled signal seek will only allow the system to stop on channels that are active. It can automatically adjust for MATV frequency offsets up to ±2MHz. There never is any programming either by the user or in the factory because the system automatically seeks to the channels that are active in its present location. There is a threshold control that allows the user to skip weak signals if he wishes. Manual fine tuning is available to increase the signal-to-noise ratio for fringe area reception or as a means of minimizing disturbing signals. Finally, the direct access channel entry is arranged to clear itself if the user is interrupted in the middle of a command.

articleTitle: The Extent and Nature of Television Reception Difficulties Associated with CB Radio Transmissions
abstract: The Federal Communications Commission's (FCC), Field Operations Bureau (FOB) has released the results of a study on interference with television reception associated with Citizens Band Radio. 1/

articleTitle: MOS Processes
Citizens Band Expansion and the Consumer Environment
abstract: Six interference modes affecting standard television and FM broadcast receivers: Rectification, Harmonics, Intermodulation, IF Beats, Images, and IF Feedthrough are examined. A map is derived showing the relationship between interference modes and broadcast channels for transmitter frequencies below 900 MHz. Harmonic relationships to aircraft bands are also considered. Two bands presently allocated to the Fixed and Mobile radio service, 48 to 50 MHz and 410 to 420 MHz, are recommended as potential sites for CB expansion.

articleTitle: Perspectives on Small, Flat Video Displays
abstract: Much work has been done during the past ten years on the development of flat displays for television (1). The flat-panel display warrants attention in that it does not possess some of the inherent limitations of the cathode ray tube (CRT). The flat panel display will be lighter and less bulky than the CRT and will not require a 25 KV power supply. The flat-panel display also has the potential of being made in any size, conceivably from 1 in.2 to sizes larger than 15 ft.2. The CRT, however, is limited to a practical screen size of 4 ft.2. Also, for small screen sizes, the CRT consumes too much power for prolonged battery operation and cannot be made much smaller than 10 in.2. The flat panel will not possess the large fragile glass envelope of the CRT making it better suited for rugged portable operation.

articleTitle: Second Generation IC's for Color TV Receivers (Part I)
abstract: Second Generation IC's with high performances for color TV's have newly been developed and now put into actual use. The IC's consist of five big IC's, which are for VIF, SIF audio, video chroma, jungle and vertical and horizontal oscillators, and vertical output. abstract: This index covers all technical items - papers, correspondence, reviews, etc. - that appeared in this periodical during the year, and items from previous years that were commented upon or corrected in this year. Departments and other items may also be covered if they have been judged to have archival value. The Author Index contains the primary entry for each item, listed under the first author's name. The primary entry includes the coauthors' names, the title of the paper or other item, and its location, specified by the publication abbreviation, year, month, and inclusive pagination. The Subject Index contains entries describing the item under all appropriate subject headings, plus the first author's name, the publication abbreviation, month, and year, and inclusive pages. Note that the item title is found only under the primary entry in the Author Index.

articleTitle: 1977 Index IEEE Transactions on Consumer Electronics Vol. CE-23
abstract: This index covers all technical items - papers, correspondence, reviews, etc. - that appeared in this periodical during the year, and items from previous years that were commented upon or corrected in this year. Departments and other items may also be covered if they have been judged to have archival value. The Author Index contains the primary entry for each item, listed under the first author's name. The primary entry includes the coauthors' names, the title of the paper or other item, and its location, specified by the publication abbreviation, year, month, and inclusive pagination. The Subject Index contains entries describing the item under all appropriate subject headings, plus the first author's name, the publication abbreviation, month, and year, and inclusive pages. Note that the item title is found only under the primary entry in the Author Index.
